lab_title: Anatomy of the Human Heart and Blood Flow
top_level_objectives: Identify the key anatomical structures of the human heart.
Describe the path of blood flow through the heart's chambers and valves.
Explain the concept of pulmonary and systemic circulation.
Relate the heart's structure, particularly the ventricular myocardium thickness, to its function.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the overall structure of the human heart.
key_visuals: A realistic 3D model of the human heart, exterior view.
Labels highlighting the major external features like the apex, base, and major coronary vessels.
student_actions: Rotate and zoom in on the 3D heart model to observe its external anatomy.
Read introductory text and listen to audio describing the heart's general location and function.

scenes.brief_purpose: Identify and understand the four chambers of the heart.
key_visuals: A 3D heart model with the outer wall removed or made transparent to reveal the four chambers.
Clearly labeled chambers: right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, left ventricle.
Visual cues (e.g., color coding) differentiating the chambers.
student_actions: Tap on each chamber to bring up its name and a brief description.
Observe the relative positions and sizes of the four chambers.

scenes.brief_purpose: Identify and locate the four heart valves.
key_visuals: The 3D heart model with emphasis on the valves between chambers and at the exit of ventricles.
Clearly labeled valves: tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral (bicuspid), aortic.
Animations or visual guides showing valve operation (opening/closing).
student_actions: Select each valve to view its name, location, and function in preventing backflow.
Watch animations of the valves in action during a simulated cardiac cycle.

scenes.brief_purpose: Identify the major blood vessels connected to the heart.
key_visuals: The 3D heart model with major vessels entering and leaving.
Labeled vessels: superior and inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, aorta.
Color coding to indicate oxygenated (red) vs. deoxygenated (blue) blood flow within vessels.
student_actions: Tap on each major vessel to identify it and learn which part of the circulation it serves.
Trace the connections of these vessels to the appropriate heart chambers.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the path of deoxygenated blood from the body to the lungs.
key_visuals: The 3D heart model with a dynamic visualization of deoxygenated blood flow.
Arrows and color changes indicating blood movement: Vena Cavae -> Right Atrium -> Tricuspid Valve -> Right Ventricle -> Pulmonary Valve -> Pulmonary Arteries -> Lungs.
Simplified lung model showing gas exchange.
student_actions: Follow the highlighted pathway of deoxygenated blood through the right side of the heart and to the lungs.
Read or listen to explanations of each step in the pulmonary circuit.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the path of oxygenated blood from the lungs to the body.
key_visuals: The 3D heart model with a dynamic visualization of oxygenated blood flow.
Arrows and color changes indicating blood movement: Pulmonary Veins -> Left Atrium -> Mitral Valve -> Left Ventricle -> Aortic Valve -> Aorta -> Body.
Simplified body circulation highlighting systemic capillaries.
student_actions: Follow the highlighted pathway of oxygenated blood through the left side of the heart and to the rest of the body.
Read or listen to explanations of each step in the systemic circuit.

scenes.brief_purpose: Compare the thickness of the left and right ventricular walls and relate it to function.
key_visuals: A cross-section of the heart model showing the thickness of the right and left ventricular walls.
Comparative visual elements or text labels highlighting the thicker left ventricle.
Visual representation of the pressure/resistance differences in pulmonary vs. systemic circulation.
student_actions: Observe the difference in myocardial thickness between the left and right ventricles.
Read or listen to an explanation linking the thicker left ventricle to its role in pumping blood to the entire body.
